title: pr-4721-review-scratchpad-lena-cho
content:
PR: #4721 — kv-cache: hierarchical prefix cache + batching integration

Summary:
- Large PR that reworks KV cache to be hierarchical (session-level + shared prefix cache) and adds tighter batching hooks into batching_manager.
- Goal: reduce redundant model compute in high prefix-share workloads and enable more efficient batching without increasing tail latency.

Quick take:
- Overall design makes sense; abstraction boundaries between kv_cache and batching_manager are cleaner.
- Concern: memory growth for shared-prefix cache under worst-case traffic patterns (see perf notes below).
- CI flaky tests: test_kv_eviction_policy and test_batching_race intermittently fail locally and in CI.

Files of interest:
- python/kv_cache/kv_cache.py (main changes)
- go/serving/batching_manager.go (batching hooks + new config)
- tests/test_kv_cache.py (unit tests adjusted)
- benchmarks/prefix_share_bench.toml (new benchmark config)

Review checklist (my running notes):
[ ] Security: ensure keys/identifiers not logged. Grep for fmt.Printf / logging of session IDs in go code.
[ ] Memory accounting: verify per-tenant memory cap enforced; where is eviction triggered? See kv_cache.py: L260-L320.
[ ] Concurrency: race conditions in batching_manager.go — uses RWMutex but I saw a possible double-checked load pattern without atomic.
[ ] Metrics: added cache_hit_rate_v2 metric—ensure it's exposed to prometheus and uses same label set as v1 (tenant/model/route).
[ ] Tests: flaky tests need deterministic seed; test_kv_eviction_policy relies on timings.
[ ] Rollout: flag-gated under feature flag kv_hierarchical_v2 — confirm default off for Dedicated customers until perf validated.

Inline comments / suggestions:
- kv_cache.py: suggest extracting EvictionPolicy into a separate class for easier unit testing (lots of nested logic in function).
- batching_manager.go: on line ~142 the comment mentions "maxBatchWindow ms" but code uses microseconds; normalize units and add a typed Duration.
- tests/test_kv_cache.py: replace time.sleep-based waits with explicit event hooks (use TestHarness.wait_for_eviction()).

Performance notes (from running local bench):
- baseline (main): 1.0x cost per token, p95 latency 85ms
- with hierarchical v2 enabled: cost 0.78x for prefix-heavy workload (high saving), but p99 increased from 220ms -> 310ms in certain bursts.
- memory high-water mark: +40% under long-lived sessions with many unique prefixes.

Open questions to ask author (Samir):
- What's the intended eviction policy for shared-prefix cache vs session cache? LRU, TTL, or size-based? The docstring is ambiguous.
- Why is the shared cache sharded by tenant rather than by model? Could this increase duplication when customers use many models?
- Can we add an integration test simulating multi-tenant random-prefix churn to catch memory regressions?

Follow-ups / TODOs (assignments):
- [Samir] Add explicit per-tenant memory cap check in kv_cache and unit test (JIRA RINF-1589).
- [Ethan] Rework batching_manager locking and add atomic pointers for currentBatch to avoid races (PR comment 7).
- [Lena] Add benchmark harness for multi-tenant churn and upload results to Confluence (page linked above).
- [Team] Gate rollout for Dedicated customers until we have production perf dashboard (tag: rollout-qa).

Notes to self / scratch:
- Might be worth splitting PR into two: 1) pure cache hierarchy + tests, 2) batching integration. Too big now.
- Local repro steps for flaky test:
  1) tox -e py38 tests/test_kv_cache.py::TestKV::test_kv_eviction_policy -k fast
  2) run with PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER_COUNT=1
  3) add -s and watch eviction log lines

Potential breaking changes (call out in release notes):
- Metrics rename cache_hit_rate -> cache_hit_rate_v2 (ensure compatibility by exporting both for a cycle).
- Config schema change: batching.window_ms -> batching.window (Duration string). Update helm chart values.yaml.

Suggested small patches before merge:
- Fix unit test seeding, add TestHarness.wait_for_eviction
- Normalize duration units and add a helper parseDuration
- Add a prometheus metric label migration shim

Risks:
- Memory blowups under pathological patterns (large number of prefixes per session)
- Increased tail latency during high burst traffic due to batch composition delays
- Possible data race in batching_manager.go leading to panics under stress

Acceptance criteria before merge:
- [ ] CI green for 3 consecutive runs
- [ ] Add one integration test for multi-tenant churn
- [ ] Confirm no memory regressed in benchmark (<=+10% HWM) or add config to limit
- [ ] Document rollover + migration notes for metrics and config

Links and references:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-serving/pull/1234 (previous kv cache attempt)
- Design doc: Confluence page (link above)
- JIRA: RINF-1589 (per-tenant memory caps)

Final thought: good improvement overall but too many moving parts for a single PR — request splitting into smaller, reviewable pieces or add clear integration tests and canary rollout plan.

-- lena
